summary.intent: Continue the Callisto release-tooling hardening roadmap: ship the 0.10.3 release, then do post-0.10.3 work (refactors, fixes, W1/W3/W4/W10/D01 planning), parallelized and stacked as PRs with minimal conflicts.
summary.outcome: Shipped and stacked many PRs (#205-#209 stack, #211 review fixes, #213 SYS-BARRIER, #214 walk.rs split, #216 W1 attestation CI job), verified 0.10.3 published, ran a Wave 0 workflow yielding verified W4 audit and wire-compat matrix, and committed the wire-compat doc as PR A with B (redaction list) and C (E176 cause) designed but not yet built.

repo: `just ci` is the full gate (includes workflow contract and policy checks) and takes ~4-5 min; must run one at a time across worktrees, cold worktrees need a full rebuild.
Squash merges mean upper stack PRs need `main` merged in after the bottom lands; conflicts arose when #202 edited a test block that #205 moved out of init.rs.
Register docs (V1-FINDINGS.md, ROAD-TO-V1.md, V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json, V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md) conflict easily across PRs; lanes should avoid them and a docs PR should prune shipped rows.
Fake-tool test harness hid the 0.10.1 regression; validate releases with real cargo/gh/git ls-remote dry runs at the release commit.
The runner's credential removal list deliberately omits NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG because generated npm auth config is delivered through it; the lists should not be naively merged.
Only the model's `known_credential_env_values` redaction list is incomplete (missing NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN, PYPI_TOKEN, CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG, TWINE_USERNAME).
Wire versions: decision writes 2/reads 1,2; intent 5 only (E215); envelope 3 only; receipt 2 only; snapshot and artifact manifest have no decode gate.
E176 drops the indeterminate cause entirely; the ProviderIndeterminateCause enum is closed and Copy, so carrying it is redaction-safe.
macOS bash lacks `mapfile`, so generated workflow templates must use portable loops.
The intent omits `artifactSlots` when empty, so jq `.artifactSlots[]` iterates null; dry-run report flattens intent with envelope fields.

code.finding: One matching non-yanked file yields Exact, which is the W3 partial-upload defect.
redact_known_secrets only replaces known secrets, so a missed name leaks.
RewriteKey distinguishes manifest, name and dependency kind but not target declarations (W10a).
Publisher rebuilds inside the effect and uploads a broad dist/ glob, not bound to the sealed intent.

friction: Review fixes for #202 weren't pushed before it merged, requiring a separate follow-up PR #211.
Stack base #205 conflicted with main after #202 merged.
I wrongly told the user #210 was awaiting checks when it had already been merged.
GitHub timed out on `gh release list` and `git fetch`, so tags couldn't be confirmed.
Negative-control real-tool run first tripped an unrelated repo-mismatch guard.
Cold build in a new worktree made the docs PR gate slow, blocking further edits.
Earlier claims needed correction: 'four credential lists drifted' overstated, and Codex review corrected the fork-PR token claim.
open_items: Merge #213 and #214 (user action); then start W10a/W10b and W9a/W9b stacks.
Build PR B (shared secret-name list plus guard test) and PR C (E176 cause, PyPI ProviderStatus) on top of PR A and link with gh stack.
W1 #216 unproven against CI's contents: read token; may need attestations: read.
D01 decisions (historical owner join, wire matrix policy) block W8, W9c/d and W3/W4 code.
W3 trusted output inventory and retry retention design.
W0 branch deletion: ~40 safe local, 11 remote, 6 need user decision.
Wire Timeout variant and add Unauthorized/RateLimited/Unreachable causes later.
Python dev groups cascade decision remains separate.
Lightweight hand-made tag at HEAD fails with E167 until next commit.
Local plan file W4 brief still references nonexistent redact_native_output.
